what_its_for: Alogliptin is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your body release more insulin after meals and reducing the amount of sugar your liver makes. It is used along with diet and exercise to keep your blood sugar in a healthy range.
how_to_take: Take alogliptin by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual dose for most adults is 25 mg once daily. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may lower your dose to 12.5 mg or 6.25 mg once daily. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed and do not change it on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store alogliptin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Store it in a dry place, such as a medicine cabinet, and keep it out of the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar levels unpredictably. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new over-the-counter medicines, herbal supplements, or vitamins, as some can raise or lower your blood sugar. Avoid skipping meals, which can cause your blood sugar to drop too low, especially if you take other diabetes medicines.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe pain in your stomach, back, or belly that does not go away (could be a sign of pancreatitis); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue, or difficulty breathing; joint pain that is severe or does not improve; signs of heart failure such as shortness of breath, sudden weight gain, or swelling of the legs or feet; blistering or peeling skin; or symptoms of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion.
when_it_works: Alogliptin begins working within a few hours of taking your first dose. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit on your blood sugar levels. Your doctor will check your A1C (a 3-month blood sugar average) and fasting blood sugar regularly to see how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will adjust your dose if you have moderate or severe kidney disease. This medicine is not recommended for people on dialysis. Older adults (65 and over): Alogliptin can be used in older adults, but your doctor may monitor you more closely for side effects. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Children: Alogliptin is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age. Liver problems: Alogliptin should not be used if you have severe liver disease.
